trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park on SR 706, follow Paradise Road east through Longmire and on for 12 more miles to the Paradise parking area. The road above Longmire is gated overnight from late October through the winter.
approach: From the Paradise (Skyline Trail) trailhead, follow the Skyline Trail to Glacier Vista and rope up to cross the Nisqually Glacier, then continue up toward the bivouac ledges near 9,300 ft. Cross the lower Kautz Glacier, climb the Kautz Cleaver, and traverse into the couloir, where the long snow ramp of the climb begins. Other ways in start from Van Trump Meadows or the Westside Road.

trailheadDirection: From Enumclaw take SR 410 east about 43 miles to the park's White River entrance, then turn right on Sunrise Road for about 5 miles. After crossing the river, turn left on White River Road, which ends at the campground. As of late October 2026 White River Road and Sunrise Road are both closed for the season.
approach: From White River Campground, take the Glacier Basin trail about 3 miles to treeline and the basin near 6,000 ft. Continue over the crevassed Inter Glacier to Camp Curtis at 8,500 ft, drop onto the Emmons Glacier and make a short climb to Camp Schurman at 9,450 ft. The climb starts from that camp, heading up and to the left on the Corridor ramp.

trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park on SR 706, follow Paradise Road east through Longmire and on for 12 more miles to the Paradise parking area. The road above Longmire is gated overnight from late October through the winter.
approach: From the Paradise (Skyline Trail) trailhead, climb the Skyline Trail past Glacier Vista, turn off at the signs for Pebble Creek and Camp Muir and go up the Muir Snowfield to Camp Muir at about 10,080 ft. Rope up there and reach the Ingraham Glacier either over Cathedral Cap or through the shorter, steeper Cadaver Gap. Walk to Ingraham Flats at about 11,100 ft, where the route proper begins.

trailheadDirection: From the Nisqually entrance of Mount Rainier National Park on SR 706, follow Paradise Road east through Longmire and on for 12 more miles to the Paradise parking area. The road above Longmire is gated overnight from late October through the winter.
approach: From the Paradise (Skyline Trail) trailhead, walk about 1 mile to Glacier Vista at 6,336 ft, rope up and head northwest across the Nisqually Glacier. Reach the Wilson Glacier by the Fan chute, by the Nisqually cutoff ramp, or early in the season straight up the Nisqually. The climb is reached from a high camp near 9,200 ft. Icefall from the Kautz ice cliff threatens the approach, and the Fan chute is exposed to rockfall.

trailheadDirection: From I-90 Exit 47 (Denny Creek and Tinkham Road), turn left over the freeway, then 0.2 mile ahead turn right onto FR 58. Pass under the freeway, turn left after 0.2 mile, and continue 2.9 miles; the parking lots are on the right, about half a mile beyond Denny Creek Campground.
approach: From the Denny Creek Trailhead (I-90 Exit 47), follow the Denny Creek trail past the water slide and Keekwulee Falls up to Hemlock Pass, 3.8 miles in, then drop to Melakwa Lake at 4.2 miles. The west face of Bryant Peak is in view from the lake; walk directly west toward it to the fattest ice flow in the middle of the face, where the climb begins.

trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
trailheadDirection: From Interstate 90 exit 34, turn left onto 468th Street to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, turn right and drive about 12 miles, passing the large Middle Fork parking area on the right. Just after the big concrete bridge turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap and follow the potholed road about 5 to 6 miles to the gate and trailhead.
approach: From the Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road), follow the Dingford Creek Trail up the valley past the Goat Creek crossing and the Myrtle Lake junction (stay right), about 5.5 to 6 miles to Hester Lake. The upper trail is partly washed out, so expect brush. Go around the north side of the lake to Little Hester Lake, then head for the saddle northwest of it, which puts you on the ridge where the climb begins.

trailheadDirection: From Darrington, drive about 16 miles south on the Mountain Loop Highway to the left turn onto Sloan Creek Road (FR 49), then follow FR 49 about 6.5 miles to the trailhead, which is on the left.
approach: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead, hike the North Fork Sauk Trail about 5 miles to Mackinaw, then about 3.5 miles of climbing to the Pacific Crest Trail and a half mile on to White Pass. Head east on the Foam Creek Trail for about 2 miles, cross the saddle to the north near 6,600 feet, then traverse the White Chuck Glacier basin northeast to Glacier Gap at roughly 7,300 feet. The approach to Gerdine Ridge and Cool Glacier ends at this gap.
